items.rationale: The calls read 1,000 + 1,500 + 2,000 + 2,500 = 7,000 tokens, because each call re-reads everything before it. An answer of 2,500 counts only the last call, and 2,500 is not the total billed.

A new run is built from the system prompt, tool descriptions and the new message; nothing from Monday persists unless the program saved it. Models do not learn from conversations, and the window is rebuilt for each run.
The model reads only its context. The program loads the saved note and inserts its text there; the model cannot open files or recall past users on its own.

Every later call re-sends the dump, so replacing it with a short note of what mattered cuts the cost of all ten calls while keeping the needed information (clearing old tool results). A larger window or a brevity instruction does not remove the tokens being re-sent.

Keyword search misses differently worded text; searching by meaning finds passages with the same meaning whatever the wording. Context size, prompt length and guessing page numbers do not fix a retrieval failure.
